en.topic: Term 1 review: sentences, punctuation and narrative writing

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: The dog barked, and the cat ran.
When the dog barked, the cat ran.
The dog barked because it was hungry.
questions.hint: A simple sentence has one main clause.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a compound sentence?
options: I was tired, but I finished my homework.
Although I was tired, I finished my homework.
questions.answer: I was tired, but I finished my homework.
questions.hint: Look for two main clauses joined by and, but or so.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: Although it was raining, we went outside.
It was raining, so we stayed in.
questions.answer: Although it was raining, we went outside.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence contains a comma splice?
options: It was late, we went home.
It was late, so we went home.
It was late; we went home.
Because it was late, we went home.
questions.answer: It was late, we went home.
questions.hint: A comma splice joins two main clauses with only a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The sun set; the sky turned orange.
The sun; set the sky turned orange.
The sun set the; sky turned orange.
